BAS2-01.note: Fronting 'for the summer program' is unnatural without a comma.

alternatives: every player | expects | the coach | to bring | their own water bottle
BAS2-02.note: Swapping the two NPs works because singular 'their' can refer to the coach, and the players expecting the coach to bring his own bottle makes sense.

alternatives: my grandfather | could convince | nobody | to replace | his old phone
BAS2-03.note: Swapping the NPs gives a grammatical sentence that makes sense: grandfather could not persuade anyone to replace his phone. It sounds slightly formal but is acceptable.

alternatives: she | got | to help | her brother | with the move
BAS2-05.note: 'got to help her brother' (got the chance to help) is fully natural.

BAS2-06.note: 'not only' is fixed inside the 'not only free' chip, so the coordinated parts cannot be swapped.

BAS2-10.note: Marginal: 'whether the store is still open I wonder' (topicalized, needs a comma).

BAS2-11.note: Marginal: 'why the meeting was cancelled nobody knows' (topicalization; acceptable in speech but normally written with a comma).

BAS2-12.note: Marginal: 'how the ancient bridge was built the guide explained' (topicalized, needs a comma).

BAS2-13.note: Marginal/archaic: 'my neighbor it was who found the lost keys'.

BAS2-14.note: Marginal/archaic: 'in this room it was that the treaty was signed'.

BAS2-15.note: Marginal: 'to play the violin takes years of practice learning' and 'learning the violin takes years of practice to play' are both odd.

BAS2-17.note: Marginal: 'my parents grew up where the village has no hospital' is grammatical but semantically odd.

alternatives: the instructor | must contact | students | who miss | the deadline
BAS2-18.note: Swapping subject and object gives a fully natural sentence.

BAS2-19.note: The swapped version ('his manager did not satisfy the excuse...') makes no sense.

BAS2-20.note: Marginal: 'are required to show to the guard their tickets' (heavy-NP shift, but the object is not heavy enough).

alternatives: researchers | discovered | that | without oxygen | the bacteria | could survive
BAS2-22.note: Fronting the adverbial inside the that-clause is grammatical and natural. Also 'the bacteria discovered that researchers could survive without oxygen' is grammatical but absurd, so it is not listed.

alternatives: the speed | of the recovery | was | what | surprised | everyone
BAS2-23.note: The reversed pseudo-cleft is fully natural.

BAS2-24.note: 'the weather depends on whether the plan will work' is grammatical but semantically absurd.

BAS2-30.note: Marginal: 'this early my brother is not used to waking up'.

BAS2-31.note: There is no 'for' chip, so 'it took three months ...' cannot be built.

BAS2-35.note: Marginal: 'the mail carrier kept barking at the neighbors' dog' is grammatical but only works as a joke.

alternatives: my first summer job | always reminds | me | of | that song
BAS2-38.note: Swapping the NPs is fully natural: the job reminds me of the song.

BAS2-44.note: Marginal: 'for the whole family my grandmother used to sew dresses' (topicalized, wants a comma).

BAS2-45.note: 'I seen' is a single chip, so inversion leaves no other order.
